rv.q: Radio Golf may not be the deepest volume on Wilson's shelf but is his most accessible, most structurally focused and most unambiguously political.
Mr. Wilson's final play is a fitting capstone to his decade-by-decade chronicle of black American life in the 20th century, though it lacks the theatrical fire of his greatest works.
But that melancholy note also brings a dramatic cost.
Pittsburgh, it would seem, has been stripped of its poetry.
This smart, resonant and solidly entertaining production was worth the wait.
Radio Golf is a fitting capstone to Wilson's cycle, a play that looks both backward and forward while standing confidently in its own present.

An immensely entertaining Radio Golf, the final play by the late great playwright August Wilson has arrived on Broadway in a handsomely staged production by Kenny Leon that bristles with forceful urgency.
